Class StackAdapterTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.StackAdapterTest
public class StackAdapterTest extends Object
Summary: This Test Suite aims to test the functionalities of the StackAdapter class. The suite is divided into sections using comments to categorize tests covering Stack-specific operations and HCollection/HList inherited methods, ensuring full compatibility with the J2SE 1.4.2 collections framework.
  • Test Case Design: The tests have been developed following the Test Driven Development methodology, meaning they were implemented before their respective methods. The test cases are designed to verify standard behaviors, boundary conditions, multiple types, and exception handling. The goal is to make sure the adaptee works exactly like a 1.4.2 Stack.

Conventions used in the documentation of the tests:

  • Every test starts from the same state: setUp() creates a new, empty StackAdapter (stackTest) before each test, so the Pre-Condition of every test is an empty stack and all the elements used are inserted by the test itself (as described in its Test Description).
  • The content of a stack is written from the bottom (index 0) to the top, e.g. [A, B] means that "A" was pushed first and "B" is on top. The iterators traverse the stack in the same order.

  • Method Details

    • setUp

      public void setUp()
      Creates a new, empty StackAdapter before each test, so that every test starts from the same known state.

    • reset

      public void reset()
      Releases the reference to the stack after each test.

    • testEmptyOnNewStack

      public void testEmptyOnNewStack()
      Summary: Verifies that a newly created stack is empty.
      • Test Case Design: Checks the initial state of the data structure.
      • Test Description: Calls empty() on stackTest without inserting any element.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is still empty.
      • Expected Results: empty() returns true.

    • testEmptyOnOneElementStack

      public void testEmptyOnOneElementStack()
      Summary: Verifies that a stack containing one element is not recognized as empty.
      • Test Case Design: Boundary case: the smallest non-empty stack (one element).
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integer 1 and calls empty().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains one element: [1].
      • Expected Results: empty() returns false.

    • testEmptyOnManyElementStack

      public void testEmptyOnManyElementStack()
      Summary: Verifies that a stack containing several elements is not recognized as empty.
      • Test Case Design: Standard case: stack with more than one element.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 4, 3, 2 and 1 (1 on top) and calls empty().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains four elements: [4, 3, 2, 1].
      • Expected Results: empty() returns false.

    • testPeekOnEmptyStackThrowsException

      public void testPeekOnEmptyStackThrowsException()
      Summary: Verifies that peek() on an empty stack throws EmptyStackException.
      • Test Case Design: Exception handling: reading the top of a stack that has no elements.
      • Test Description: Calls peek() on the empty stack.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack is still empty.
      • Expected Results: A java.util.EmptyStackException is thrown.

    • testPeekOnOneElementStack

      public void testPeekOnOneElementStack()
      Summary: Verifies that peek() on a one-element stack returns that element.
      • Test Case Design: Standard return value of peek() in the smallest non-empty case.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integer 1, calls peek() and compares the returned value with 1.
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack still contains exactly one element: [1].
      • Expected Results: peek() returns the Integer 1.

    • testSizeAfterPeek

      public void testSizeAfterPeek()
      Summary: Verifies that peek() does not remove the top element.
      • Test Case Design: Checks that peek() is non-destructive by comparing the size after the call.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Integers 1, 2, 3 and 4 (4 on top), calls peek() (the returned value is ignored) and then reads size().
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.

    • testSubListModificationsReflectOnParent

      public void testSubListModificationsReflectOnParent()
      Summary: Verifies that a structural modification made through the subList is reflected on the parent stack.
      • Test Case Design: Backing between the subList view and the parent stack, using clear() on the view.
      • Test Description: Pushes the Strings "A", "B" and "C", obtains subList(1, 2) (the view [B]) and calls clear() on it; then checks the subList isEmpty() and the parent size(), get(1) and contains("B").
      • Pre-Condition: stackTest is a new, empty StackAdapter created by setUp(); no element has been inserted yet.
      • Post-Condition: The stack contains two elements: [A, C]; the subList is empty.
      • Expected Results: The subList isEmpty() returns true; the parent size() returns 2, get(1) returns "C" and contains("B") returns false.
